title: Japan's First Railway
summary: Japan's first railway ran between Shimbashi in Tokyo and Yokohama. Regular services began in June 1872 on the Shinagawa–Yokohama section, and the full line opened on 14 October 1872 in a ceremony attended by the Meiji Emperor, under the Ministry of Public Works.

uncertainty.note: Regular services between Shinagawa and Yokohama began 12 June 1872; 14 October 1872 is the opening ceremony of the full line to Shimbashi.

where.modern_name: Shimbashi Station area, Minato, Tokyo, Japan (proxy pin: the line's Tokyo terminus; the line ran to Yokohama)

importance.justification: Opening of the country's first railway, the start of Japan's national rail network.

sources.title: A Short History of Transport in Japan from Ancient Times to the Present, ch. 6 Railways
